_readme: The cloud -> robot ACTION script, and the state both SIM clients must end in.
`RemoteChatResponse.response_actions[]` is how the brain DIRECTS the robot rather
than only speaking through it -- launch a module, leave one, sleep, arm the QR
scanner, run a named on-robot function, subscribe to perception events (see
docs/reverse-engineering/protocol/remote-chat-protocol.md, section RemoteChatAction).
DoD criterion 4 says the two SIM clients are interchangeable; on this channel that
was false until 2026-09-03: `sim/web/bridge.js::applyAction` acted on actions and
`sim/virtual_moxie.py` ignored them entirely (grep -c response_actions -> 0).
`script` is the four remote_chat responses `sim/test_bridge.mjs` already emits at the
browser SIM (event_id act-1 .. act-4), and `expected_state` is the state that file
already asserts the browser reached. So this golden is held from BOTH ends:
sim/tests/test_actions_reach_the_robot.py  the SIL robot reaches expected_state
sim/test_bridge.mjs                        the browser SIM reaches the same state
sim/tests/test_sim_client_parity.py        both clients name the same verbs and
report the same stat keys
so neither client can start disagreeing about what an action MEANT without a test
going red. Regenerate: drive VirtualMoxie._on_chat_reply over `script` and dump
`action_stats()`.
`execute_script` / `execute_expected` are the second half, added 2026-09-04. PR #119
put `function_id` (proto field 7), `function_args` (8) and `action_args` (10) on the
wire, and `sim/web/bridge.js::applyAction` read `entry.function` alone and no args at
all -- so our own server's named `execute` rendered in the browser as `(unnamed)`
while the SIL robot named it. The two clients disagreed about the one verb that had
just gained a payload. `execute_script` drives BOTH clients over the four responses
that exercise every spelling (list args, mapping args, the SIM's older `function`,
an unnamed execute, unreadable args, and args on a non-execute verb) and
`execute_expected` is the decode both must reach, projected onto `applied_keys`.
Held from both ends the same way `script` is:
sim/tests/test_sim_client_parity.py  the SIL robot reaches execute_expected, and
bridge.js reads the same names in the same
precedence order
sim/test_action_payload.mjs          the REAL bridge.js, driven over this script,
reaches execute_expected -- with a negative
control that reverts the fix and must fail
`args` is therefore no longer in `client_only_keys`: both clients record it, under
that name, and `applied_keys` is where it now lives.

script._why: a launch: the brain puts the child in an activity
an action-LESS entry carrying only an event subscription -- legal, not an error; the legacy singular mirrors it and must not fire twice
a verb this client does not implement, and a junk entry: both COUNTED and skipped, never raised -- a future server verb may not break an old client's turn
goodbye: leave the module and go to sleep, two actions on one response

execute_script._why: the contract's spelling -- function_id (proto field 7) + function_args (field 8, repeated string), which is what wire.py::encode_action emits for a LIST of args
a MAPPING of args rides action_args (field 10, repeated ActionArgsEntry{key,value}) -- encode_action picks the home by TYPE, so a client must decode both and invent no third convention
the SIM's own older `function` spelling stays accepted, and function_id WINS when both are present -- a client that only understood the one server it was written against would not be a client

an execute with nothing to read records "" and [] rather than a guess; an unreadable action_args falls THROUGH rather than recording an empty object as if the brain had sent one; and args are not execute-only on the wire, so a launch that carries them keeps them

a MALFORMED function_args is still PRESENT, and presence is what decides the fall-through: a client that tested falsiness instead of absence would silently promote the action_args underneath it and the two clients would record different arguments for the same message. Both record what field 8 actually held.
